en: The Secret Essence of the Crown.
Hariḥ oṃ.
Śrī Pārvatī said: O Śrī Pārvatī said:
O Cidambara, Great Bliss, Performer who displays the dance!
This is indeed the secret of secrets, the Yantra of the five-syllabled [mantra]. || 1 ||
O Lord, the conjunction and separation of our two wheels is eternal for the sake of protecting the world; it is my protective mechanism. || 2 ||
"Tell me truly that state which has not been declared to anyone.
The Lord said: "The great yantra called the Śrīsabhā is the manifestation of my own form."
O Goddess, the secret of secrets is the Cakra, which is identical with you;
I am the manifest five-syllabled mantra, while you are the fifteen-syllabled one.
I am the nine-syllabled one in person, and you, O Goddess, are the ninefold self;
our union of the wheels is beyond the reach of Viṣṇu and the other gods.
Out of affection for you, I shall explain the characteristics of the *cakra* grid, its measurement, its arrangement, and its specific distinctions in detail.
O Mahāgaurī, listen with an attentive mind to the mantra-yoga;
having reached the station of the consciousness-ether (cidambara), one should enter the temple of the mantra.

Having entered [the temple] and facing north, one should meditate upon the Guru with a concentrated mind. (In Cidambaram, verse 7, the Yantra is drawn and worshipped; this is therefore likely where it was redacted.)
Meditating on the Self as serene within the ether of consciousness, like a reflection in a mirror.
One should meditate upon Gaurī in that manner, as if in a stainless mirror of the mind;
having adorned one's own body, which is the embodiment of the mantra, with perfumes and other offerings.
O Great Goddess, within the pure sky of consciousness in the stainless mind, you see me— the formless, stainless, and eternal bliss— dancing there.
Having mentally worshipped you, O Goddess, who abide independently on the left side, whose nature is consciousness, and who are the witness of all, with sixteen forms and movements; || 11 ||
O beloved, just as a goddess [is seen] on the northern side of a palace, so too is great devotion, whose nature is illusory, situated upon the wall of the mind within the structure of the heart. 12.
For she is the supreme Śivā, whose body is eternally made manifest for the sake of protecting the world, who dwells within the Great Heart (Mahāhṛdaya) in the form of a dancing figure.
"O Goddess, having correctly seen [the mandala] belonging to you and me, as well as in the *Yāmala* and the *Svatantraka*,
and having properly seen the grid (*prasthāra*) which is the embodiment of the mantra,
one should draw the forms of us two in the wheel according to the rule, O beloved."
Having first established the Brahma-line and the circular line with a clear mind, [the temple] should be ninety-six finger-breadths in length and its width should be equal to that.
O Dear One, having divided it into forty parts, the sixteenth among them is the middle one.
From the Veda, they say, O Goddess, you are the Embodiment and the Intellect, whose nature consists of the qualities;
the first is independent, while the other is the Yāmala, whose essence is Śiva.
The independent [measurement] is said to be of two kinds, consisting of sixty-two finger-breadths. The goddess, the garland, and its own pericarp should be divided tenfold. (18)
Having praised the Goddess, Gaṅgā, and Vallī in due order, one should cast nine threads across and wipe the sides of the nine [squares]. 19.

One should rub the beginning and the end with that which stands between them, and the middle with that which stands between them; likewise, one should rub the middle with that which follows it, according to the respective portions of the qualities.
In the fourth [figure], the ninth and the fifth go to the third;
in the second, having touched the ninth.
The sixth [syllable] should go to the second [position], and the eighth should go to the first.
The seventh is called the remainder of the meter; the powers are said to be the fifth.
The first, having touched the seventh, becomes the fourth and the eighth.
Having touched the second and the ninth [lines], one should likewise proceed to the third;
in this manner, one should apply the ritual lines on both sides of the thread.
Moving in this manner, O Dear One, one should observe the fire and place it; having touched the circle, one places the hexagon, and without touching that, the octagon.
O Goddess, one should cast the lines across the center of the middle triangle and along the sides; then, at the ends, one should cast the lines in due order so that it becomes a sixteen-sided figure.
A wheel with fourteen spokes, two wheels each with ten spokes, an eight-sided figure, and a triangle—there is no doubt that these lead to the attainment of success. || 26 ||
Thus, O Supreme Goddess, having fashioned the arrangement of your wheel,
fashion my wheel beyond your wheel.
Having made it square with a length of ninety-six finger-breadths and a width equal to that,
one should divide it into thirty-two parts for the Lord.
Having divided the two feet into four equal parts, the wise one should draw threads all around; within that [space], there is a square.
O Dear One, having divided it into eighteen parts, one should divide the middle of that;
having made the vertical dimension one-sixteenth part, the horizontal [dimension] should be seventeen parts.
Starting from the southern line, the ninth [line] shall be the middle one;
starting from the western line, the ninth [line] shall be the middle one. || 30 ||
One should not strike the lines during the division; rather, by this very method, one should rotate that mandala from the center through the six and a half directional squares.
O Dear One, one should rotate the maṇḍala outside that by one and a half padas;
outside of that, there should be two maṇḍalas measuring three, four, and five finger-breadths respectively.
At the time of the inner mandala, however, one should perform the mandala with only half a step;
indeed, within the three mandalas, one should cause the mandala to revolve.
One should wipe away the branches situated in the middle of the three mandalas,
so that the earth consists of nine sections and is not of a fragmented nature.
One should conceive of the central section of the great street as the earth, the heart-lotus; and the squares situated at the corners for the purpose of the arrays (vyūha). || 35 ||
Having divided the five lines in the middle into four [sections],
let there always be five [lines] drawn transversely from the southeast (Agni) to the northeast (Īśāna).
One should draw [the letters] in those squares, starting from the southeast and ending in the northeast.
In the arrays, according to the rule of instruction, there are five syllables each;
and as for the letter *śa* and the letter *na*, which have been proclaimed by me— (37)
One should indeed place the syllable *na* at the beginning of *Yama*, the syllable *pa* at the beginning of *Pāśin*, and the *praṇava* (*oṃ*) itself;
in the middle of that, one should place the syllables *na*, *ya*, and *ma*.
And one should not write the fivefold self; rather, one should then place the *śikhā*.
They say "to Māvasineya" is the *āgneya*; this is the fivefold pentad.
Now I shall describe specifically the rite for the southwestern petal (nairṛtadala), which is neither Yañca nor Mañca, neither Śivāna nor Vāmaśika. || 40 ||
They say "Salutation to Śiva," and likewise for those who possess the *ma* and *śa*.
And the letter *va* and the letter *na*, in sequence at the ends of the *ma* and *śa* syllables. || 41 ||
"The petal in the southwest belongs to Nairṛta"—thus [it is known] from the tradition of the venerable Guru.
Now, furthermore, I shall declare this mantra-graha of the Guru in the northwest.
There is no "ś" ending after "mavāya," nor is there "yanavāśi" or "ma" itself; after "nama śivāya," there is neither the letter "v" nor "śimaya. (43)
The letter *śa*, the letter *ya*, and the ninth [letter *na*] among them, in sequence—this is declared to be the *avagraha*; in the northwest, there are five groups of five.
The syllable *śi* and the syllable *na*, together with the syllable *ma* completed;
then *nama śivāya*, followed by the syllables *ma* and *ya*. (45)
Having written the Praṇava (Om) in the center, the wise one should write "na" in its middle; having placed two "va" syllables on the two sides, he should likewise place the letter "ma" and "śi".
Ending with "Obeisance to Śiva," one should strike the Īśāna [corner] five times each;
then, one should mark the subsidiary lines across and upwards from the center.
O skillful one, these vertical lines (ūrdhvasūtra) are at the sixth foot, at the seventh foot,
and at half the seventh; likewise, they are at one-third of the eighth and at half of the ninth and tenth.
One should then lay down these vertical lines starting from the back,
at the fourth part of the fifth [section], at the seventh, and at the half of the eighth.
Furthermore, in the eighth part, in the half-part, again in the tenth step,
in the one-third part of a single step, and in the fourteenth step.
In this manner, one should gradually draw lines across from the south;
and at the fourth part of the southern side, there stands the tip of the raised *arghya* vessel.
The tip of the thumb of the swinging hand, extending as far as the wrist, and reaching inward to the base of the palm, constitutes the *ḍamaruka* hand gesture. (52)
In the *Ṣaṣṭhīrdhapādasūtra*, however, O fair-faced one, the ankle is raised by two units,
while the wrist and the hanging hand are likewise [measured] at one unit each.
With the feet raised up to the knees, one should quickly [perform the rite] starting from seven steps;
[the mudrā] of Abhaya consists of the wrist up to the palm of the hand.
O Dear One, the seventh [hand] with three fingers is placed upon the knee;
it is carved so that the tips of the fingers rest on the left [knee], ending at the thumb in the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya).
The ninth thread begins at the middle of the luster of the ankle and the hiccup;
it remains on the ninth thread, extending as far as the heel.
The swinging line (ḍolā) extends as far as the left shoulder, ending at the outer corner of the eye;
starting from the tenth [mark], it reaches the middle of the palm of that hand along the thread.
Furthermore, with the toes curled upward,
the space between the two heels should be such that the buttocks do not touch the ground in the eighth half-part [of the body].
But in the Daśamārddhaka Sūtra, it is said to be situated between the two elbows.
O fair-faced one, [one should mark] the half-knee, the copper-colored [portion], and the navel;
(having thus performed what arises from the sūtras, as well as the specific details according to the scriptures,
|| 57 ||) at the twelfth part, however, are the *hikkā* and the two wrists (*maṇibandhaka*).
But in the thirteen-and-a-half-finger thread, O beloved, [the point] between the two eyes is the middle.
The limit of Tūṣṇīśa is at one-fourteenth part from above;
thus, having performed the work arising from the thread up to the specific end according to the thread.

O beloved Goddess of the gods, one should display the inner circle, which possesses the splendor of fire-rays, by reciting [the mantra] twenty-one times; and one should likewise display the rays. || 1 ||
Or [the letters] *varṇa*, or *puṣpikā*, or even *savarṇāpuṣpikā*. || 2 ||
One should draw this wheel on the outer mandala precisely in a clockwise direction; O Mahāgaurī, it reveals my very form. (3)
In this manner, the artisan, following the path of the scriptures, must perform the filling of the minor limbs within the center of the earth-heart (madhyahṛdaya) of the joined wheel of time.
O Dear One, my *Yāmala* has been proclaimed from the *Svatantra*;
it consists of all the gods, is the lotus encircled by radiance, and is rooted in the foundation.
One should [visualize] the bulb, the stalk, the filaments, and the pericarp in sequence;
[the lotus] is endowed with all five [elements] beginning with Earth, and the mantra is accompanied by the sacred revelation (śruti).
O beloved, having drawn an eight-petalled lotus with the luster of a pericarp,
O Great Goddess, this lotus is fashioned from the lotus of the mantra.
One should place the Praṇava in the center of the pericarp and the syllable Māyā outside;
there are twenty-two lines, with the Praṇava in the middle and on the left.
In those squares, one should write the six-syllabled mantra, placing each syllable one by one in a clockwise direction; thus, the Prasāda-mantra becomes six-syllabled.
O Dear One, [one should recite] "vāśinamaya vāśiśca namayañca satārakam," and then again "namaḥ śivāya," ending with the Praṇava (Om).
Having first placed the syllable *śi* within the *praṇava*, this is the vow of *māyā*;
having then placed the five-syllabled mantra in the middle of the *praṇava* and the *mālā*.
Having thus arranged the lotus of the mantra, one should place it upon the lotus;
in each of the three steps, one should remember the syllable of Māyā (Hrīṃ), which is the very form of Māyā. 2.
O beloved, truth indeed serves as the defining characteristic of the world;
therefore, presided over by that [truth], one should delineate the form of the mantra in its respective locations according to what is appropriate.
From the head down to the feet, and even in every limb and sub-limb,
[one should assign] the letters from 'a' to 'kṣa', beginning with the Praṇava (Om) and ending with 'Namaḥ'.
Having joined them together, one should place the great mantra of the goddess Āmrakāntā;
one should place the nine-syllable life-mantra of the secret mantra.
One should place the five syllables in their respective locations according to the prescribed method:
the letter *ya* should be on the thumb, and one should place the letter *va* on the index finger.
The syllable ŚI should be on the middle finger, MA on the ring finger, and NA on the little finger; the syllable RAU belongs to the Mistress (Īśvarī) by way of emanation.
One should assign the five syllables from the thumb to the little finger on the feet and hands, and [the remaining syllables] to the ankles,
wrists, shanks, knees, thighs, and the region of the genitals.

O Dear One, having placed the six syllables upon the hips and the back, as well as the syllable *yaṃ* and the *praṇava* in the belly and the navel according to their proper application, one should hold them evenly.
One should place the two Śivas at the navel, on the breasts, on the chest, and on the hands;
likewise, O Maheśvarī, on the arms and at the region of the elbows and the wrists.
O Śivā, one should not place the subtle pentad upon me;
the subtle pentad consists of the letter *ma*, the letter *ya*, and the letter *śi*. || 1 ||
One should place two new [drums] in the hands of the Goddess with their tips pointing toward the right;
likewise, the hand-drum (ḍamaru) and the bracelets are to be placed according to the sequence of the hips.
One should place "bhānta" on the first [finger], "ādya" on the second, and "śivāya" in due order; likewise, "nayo" and "namavo" should be placed on the tips of the fingers on the left and above.
One should visualize the fire, joined with a flame in the sky and illuminating my own light,
in the throat, the ear-bone, the mouth, and the tip of the nose, in due order.
*Namaḥ śivāya* is for the eyes, *śrīṃ* for the head, in due order;
the first *śiva* is for the middle of the eyebrows, and the intensely radiant *haṃsa* is for the center [of the heart].
O Dear One, one should place the syllable *Aṃ* joined with a bindu on each limb;
the twelve-syllable mantra on the mass of matted hair, and *Gaṃ* and *Māyā* on the left side.
One should place the syllable *dhūḥ*, the word *dhūraṃ*, and the five syllables *bilva pañca*;
then, on the right, one should place the letter ending in *j* (*ja*), joined with *nṛtyat* and the crescent moon (*candrakhaṇḍa*).
The three powers [of the breath] reside in the three joints of Apasmāra:
at the head, the forehead, the space between the eyebrows, the cheeks, the lips, the throat, and the eyes.
O Goddess, one should place the secret mantra on the navel, the throat, the thighs, and the feet;
on the two sides, the heart, the neck, the belly, the two feet, and the jaw.
O beloved, one should place the syllables of the vital breath (prāṇa) on the mouth, the eyebrows, and the forehead;
and [one should place] the Haṃsa mantra in forward and reverse order on the heart and the sides.
O Goddess, one should perform the placement of the ninefold self (navātmaka) in the foundation, the heart, the linga, the belly, the two soles of the feet, the ears, the chest, and the bindu.

Having placed [the beads] in those respective positions, one should place the garlands, which consist of the syllable *namaḥ*, even upon my own body; and the Goddess herself places the great mantra directly upon the ear.
Having thus arranged the mantras in the station that pervades the sky (vyomavyāpin),
one should then place them at the base of the light in a clockwise sequence.
One should write the twelve Vidyās that manifest my form;
O Goddess, one should install them at the base, beginning with "To Śiva," proceeding clockwise.
Twenty-one times in the five types of rites and in others as well,
one should draw [the lines] starting from the southern path in a clockwise sequence.
Then, facing [the deity], one recites "Hari Hara," followed by the five Vāruṇa syllables—
*hrīṃ*, *śrīṃ*, *aiṃ*, *haṃ*, and *saḥ*— and these in the subsequent positions.
In the preceding words, beginning with "lavarayaha," one should write the syllable "hā" using the mantra "namaḥ śivāya. || 6 ||
One should fill the four directions with the "life-syllable" (jīvākṣara); [the life-syllable being] *a, i, u, e, o*. One should write in sequence: *śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ haṃ saḥ*. (8)
Having thus arranged the mantras within my own limbs, which are identical with me,
as well as within the wheel, the Goddess should wipe away those mantras situated outside my limbs.
Then the goddess Śakti, who is identical with that [wheel], should erase the lines on the left side of the Independent One (Svatantra), as if in the playful act of observing his dance. 100.
The supreme goddess who desires Śiva, the beautiful one for him who desires Śiva;
or else, in the Vāma-yāmala, she who dwells in the midst of the circle of radiance.
O beloved, having learned from the mouth of the Guru the truth concerning you and me, as well as the union of the cakras in the abodes and the yoga of mantra according to reality; || 102 ||
O beloved of the vision, for those men who worship here according to the path declared in the scriptures, their devotion shall be eternally a giver of liberation.
I know your form, and you know my form;
O Great Goddess, you are the ocean of mantras, extracted from the milk-ocean of mantras.
One should constantly recite this king of mantras: "cidambara naṭaḥ.
O Beloved, this secret destroys sins and bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Therefore, having renounced everything, one should always recite the King of Mantras; it should be guarded with effort and not given to just anyone. 106.
It should indeed be given to one's own son, or to one who is like a son, who is righteous, steadfast, skillful, pure, and ever devoted to the Self.

Without understanding the secret meaning of the *cidambara*, even those who appear to be excellent teachers bring about misfortune; therefore, the Goddess has been bestowed upon the wise man who possesses skill.
Therefore, with every effort, this should be understood by the most excellent of teachers.
[Thus ends the third Spanda in the extraction of the Mantra-yoga from the Śrīmakuṭottararahasya.]
